- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.8) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce overshoot by 10–15% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ -0.3) and forecast is still high, apply downward bias of 5–10% to reflect market cooling.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if recent 5-day mean is below 65 and sentiment is neutral or negative, reduce forecast by 3–5% to avoid mean-reversion miss.  
- If forecast spikes >10% above recent 10-day average, apply lag correction: subtract 2–3 days of momentum to avoid overreacting to short-term noise.  
- When sentiment is volatile (±0.3–0.7) and forecast diverges >5% from true, use sentiment-weighted smoothing: average 3–5 days of sentiment to dampen erratic forecasts.
